question.text: The co-ordinate of a point on the auxiliary circle of the ellipse $x^{2}+2 y^{2}=4$ corresponding to the point on the ellipse whose eccentric angle is $60^{\circ}$ will be

solution.text: $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{2}=1$ Equation of auxiliary circle is $x^{2}+y^{2}=4$ $\therefore$ Point on the auxiliary circle is $\begin{array}{l} p\left(2 \cos 60^{\circ}, 2 \sin 60^{\circ}\right) \\ p(1, \sqrt{3}) \end{array}$
